question: The Government introduced the 'Navratna' scheme in _________ to identify and support CPSEs with competitive advantages in their journey to becoming global leaders.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1997**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **'Navratna'** scheme was introduced by the Government of India in **1997** to identify and provide greater autonomy to selected Central Public Sector Enterprises (**CPSEs**).
 
• The goal of the scheme was to enable these enterprises to compete globally and become leaders in their respective industries.
 
• Under this scheme, CPSEs that demonstrated strong financial and operational performance were granted enhanced decision-making powers.
 
• The **'Navratna' status** allows eligible CPSEs to invest up to Rs. 1,000 crore or 15% of their net worth without government approval, enabling faster decision-making.
 
• This scheme was part of the larger efforts to reform and liberalize India's public sector enterprises, aligning them with the growing competitive environment following the **1991 economic liberalization policies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Navratna CPSEs:**

 
 
• Navratna CPSEs are granted greater financial autonomy compared to other public sector enterprises.
 
• They have the freedom to form joint ventures, enter into technology agreements, and make financial investments without requiring prior government approvals.
 
• Examples of Navratna companies include Bharat Electronics Limited (**BEL**), Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (**HAL**), and Oil India Limited (**OIL**).
 
 
 
• **Maharatna and Miniratna Status:**
 
 
• In addition to Navratna, CPSEs can also achieve **Maharatna** or **Miniratna** status based on specific eligibility criteria.
 
• Maharatna CPSEs enjoy even greater financial autonomy, allowing them to make investments up to Rs. 5,000 crore without government approval.
 
• Miniratna CPSEs are categorized into **Category I** and **Category II**, offering limited autonomy based on their financial performance and profitability.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria for Navratna Status:**
 
 
• CPSEs must have a **Miniratna Category I status** and a consistent record of financial and operational excellence.
 
• They should score at least 60 out of 100 on parameters such as net profit, manpower cost, earnings per share, and the ratio of profit before depreciation, interest, and taxes to capital employed.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Navratna Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme has significantly enhanced the competitiveness of CPSEs in the global market.
 
• It has allowed these enterprises to invest in large-scale projects, modernize operations, and expand their market reach.
 
• Navratna companies have contributed substantially to India's economic growth and industrial development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **1991 Economic Reforms:**

 
 
• The Navratna scheme was part of India's broader economic reforms initiated in **1991** to liberalize the economy and reduce government intervention.
 
• These reforms aimed to make CPSEs more competitive and efficient, allowing them to operate in a market-driven environment.
 
 
 
• **Global Competitiveness:**
 
 
• Navratna status has enabled CPSEs to compete globally by providing them with the flexibility to invest in advanced technology and strategic partnerships.
 
• It has also facilitated the expansion of Indian enterprises into international markets, boosting India's presence in global trade.
